$comment: THEME = confetti (the flagship, and the default theme baked into the build). This file is the BRAND-KIT CONTRACT: the handful of input tokens a theme sets. Everything visible derives from these via the wiring in tokens/semantic/theme-roles.json (roles → inputs, emitted once under :root as var() refs). A downstream demo creates a new theme by overriding ONLY these inputs in its own [data-theme='<name>'] block — no changes to Confetti. Inputs reference primitives; neutrals (surfaces/text/borders) come from the active mode. Emitted under [data-theme='confetti'].

primary.comment: brand color — drives text.accent, primary action fill, ghost hover

accent.$comment: The four decorative 'confetti' hues (bold tone). A demo may repoint these or leave Confetti's.

syntax.$comment: The code-block surface and the two neutrals that sit on it. Deliberately on the THEME axis, not the mode axis: a snippet is an inset terminal, deep in light and dark alike, so one set of syntax colors has to read against it in both. The four accent hues above are the syntax colors — they are already tuned to carry ink on a light fill, which makes them light enough to read as text on this deep surface.

surface.comment: deepest midnight — the code block ground

shape.$comment: The theme's shape personality. control = pills/buttons, container = cards, border = the hairline outline weight.

font.$comment: The theme's typefaces. display = headings/titles, body = prose/content, label = mono UI (buttons, badges, eyebrows). A demo repoints these to change the whole system's type.

interaction.$comment: How filled buttons respond on hover. Confetti does not move, glow or cast a shadow: primary and danger lighten a step (hover-brightness), and secondary takes a subtle background (secondary-hover-brightness stays at none). The glow is reserved for cards. button-lift = the transform, held as none.

secondary-hover-brightness.comment: a secondary button changes its BACKGROUND on hover (action.secondary.fill-hover), not its lightness — brightening a near-white fill would cancel the very change we are after
